note: Which sources each measurement layer is considered to measure.
shoal-bench hashes these to decide whether a committed capture still describes the current
code. A path may be a file or a directory; a directory means every .rs file beneath it,
This list is a hand maintained approximation and it will drift. The staleness rule is built
so that drifting is safe in one direction only: the commit hash is checked first and catches
every change coarsely, and these digests can only ever narrow a 'stale' verdict to
'unaffected'. They can never turn 'stale' into 'fresh'. A path missing from this file
therefore produces a capture wrongly reported as unaffected by a change, never one wrongly
reported as fresh - and an unaffected verdict still shows how many commits have landed since.
Adding a path here changes the manifest hash, which is recorded in every capture taken
afterwards, so the change is visible rather than silent.

F8 moved the workloads out of shoal/examples/tmdb.rs and into shoal-bench/src/workloads, and the stage report builder out of shoal/src/stages.rs into the same place. The three workload layers point at that directory now. This changes the manifest hash, so every capture taken before F8 is correctly reported as no longer describing the current macro layer - which is true, and is not something to engineer around.

F10 added shoal/benches/wire.rs and the protocol module it measures to the micro layer. The client is deliberately not listed here: wire.rs exercises the framing, not the client, and shoal-core/src/client.rs is already in the macro layer. This changes the manifest hash, so every micro capture taken before F10 is correctly reported as no longer describing the current micro layer.
